records.summary: 1309 Grant Ave sits in the North Beach Neighborhood Commercial District with significant overlay restrictions on restaurant and bar alcohol service. The space is an existing restaurant (Ristorante Ideale) that has held an active Type 47 license since 2001, originally authorized in 1988 for the upgrade from Type 41 to Type 47. The records show a conditional-use posture for intensifying an existing restaurant's alcohol service in North Beach: Planning Code § 780.3(c)(2)(A) requires a CUA with a finding that the restaurant is and will remain a bona fide eating place serving at least 51% of gross receipts from food. The block is extraordinarily dense—57 food/drink businesses and 45 on-sale licenses within 500 ft—but the last five years show a 90% approval rate (N=10 dated use decisions) for comparable restaurant and bar applications nearby, nearly all continuations of existing uses or license transfers with no space expansion.

patterns.pattern: Type 47 transfers and upgrades to existing North Beach restaurants with no space expansion are routinely approved, either as continuations of existing conditional uses (via agency referral in 15–44 days) or by Conditional Use Authorization (nine months including hearing). No denials in the candidate set.

The Planning Department treats ABC license transfers (Types 41 and 47) to existing restaurants as 'continuations of existing use' when the space has not been vacant for more than 18 months and no enlargement or intensification of the physical premises is proposed, approving them administratively without a public hearing via agency referral.

All approvals for restaurant alcohol service in the North Beach NCD and SUD include or reference the requirement that the restaurant 'operate and maintain the licensed premises as a bona fide eating place,' consistent with Planning Code § 780.3(c)(2)(A)'s mandate that at least 51% of gross receipts come from food sales.

When a Conditional Use Authorization is required (not a continuation), standard conditions of approval include: signage compliance with Article 6, odor control equipment, sidewalk maintenance per DPW standards, community liaison appointment, three-year validity with diligent pursuit, and garbage/recycling/composting storage. No project-specific conditions restricting hours, occupancy, or sales mi…

The 2020 amendments to Planning Code Sections 722 and 780.3 (Ordinance 182-20, effective August 27, 2020) relaxed restrictions on Restaurant uses in the North Beach SUD, allowing certain Limited Restaurants that operated as bona fide eating places to convert to full Restaurants without a new CUA or 311 notification, and permitting Restaurant uses that were previously more restricted.

Changes of operator or DBA at an existing restaurant space in North Beach are treated as continuations of the existing conditional use when no expansion of square footage, seating, or hours occurs, and are approved by agency referral in 15–40 days rather than requiring a new CUA hearing.

risk.concept_summary: Intensifying an existing restaurant at 1309 Grant Avenue, North Beach, by upgrading from a Type 41 beer-and-wine license to a Type 47 full-bar license with no construction or space expansion.

overall.next_step: Confirm with San Francisco Planning whether the existing active Type 47 license (ABC #372058, issued 2001) is still valid for this space or whether a new Conditional Use Authorization is required for the described intensification, and confirm whether the business is part of a chain.

approvals.summary: Intensifying an existing restaurant in North Beach requires Conditional Use Authorization because Planning Code § 780.3(c)(1)(B) treats even same-use intensification as conditional, and § 178 prohibits significant alteration of a conditional use without a new CUA.

findings.text: An active ABC Type 47 license (on-sale general, eating place) is on file at 1309 Grant Avenue, issued March 5, 2001 to Ristorante Ideale. That license type is held by restaurants under Planning Code § 102, so the space is read as an existing restaurant.

The 1988 Conditional Use Authorization (Case No. 1987.801C) approved exchanging ABC License 41 to 47 and expanding an existing full-service restaurant at 1309–1311 Grant Avenue, filed December 8, 1987, approved January 28, 1988.

Planning Code § 780.3(c)(2)(A) requires a Conditional Use finding that the restaurant is and will remain a bona fide eating place serving at least 51% of gross receipts from food prepared and sold on the premises, on request submitting records of the preceding year's sales.

Nine of ten dated use decisions within 1,000 ft in the last five years were approved (three outright, six with conditions); one was withdrawn; zero were denied. The 90% approval rate (N=10) includes mostly continuations of existing restaurant uses with license transfers.

The nearest comparable Type 47 transfer to an existing restaurant (414 Columbus Avenue, 51 meters away) was approved by CUA in December 2022 after nine months, with standard conditions on signage, odor control, sidewalk maintenance, community liaison, and three-year validity; no conditions limited hours, occupancy, or food-sales percentage.

Whether the business is part of a formula-retail chain is not stated in the description. Formula retail is not permitted in the NCD-NORTH BEACH district under Planning Code § 722, so a finding that the business is formula retail would block approval.

approvals.summary: The description does not state how the Type 47 license will be obtained—by transfer from another owner, transfer from another premises, or original application—so the rules cannot determine which ABC process and public-convenience-or-necessity requirements apply.

findings.text: Census tract 106.00 has 59 active on-sale retail licenses against 12 authorized under ABC's September 2026 census tract allocations, so the tract is over-concentrated. State law tests new licenses and premises-to-premises transfers for undue concentration under Business and Professions Code § 23958.4.

Type 47 is a quota license: state law limits on-sale general licenses to one per 2,000 county inhabitants, so in counties over that ratio ABC issues no additional licenses and the applicant must purchase and transfer an existing license unless an exception applies.

ABC processes a premises-to-premises transfer of a Type 47 in 90–240 days including escrow, posting, local zoning sign-off, and any public-convenience-or-necessity review. Market prices for Type 47 licenses in San Francisco typically run $100,000–$450,000.

ABC's daily status reports do not show the status on June 7, 2023 for 15 licenses within 1,000 ft and 13 in the census tract (their status changed two or more times since); they are left out of the tract concentration count, so the true on-file count may be higher.

approvals.summary: A health permit to operate is issued after plan check and inspection without a hearing, and is allowed as of right for a restaurant with a full kitchen.

findings.text: Under California Retail Food Code §§ 114380–114381 and San Francisco Health Code Article 8, any food or drink business needs a health permit to operate, issued by the Department of Public Health after plan check and final inspection confirm the facility matches approved plans and a certified food safety manager is on staff.
The FY2026–27 fee schedule sets the Permit to Operate application at $470 (includes initial inspection) with a $0 annual license fee for restaurants and bars for 2026–28; reinspections are $276/hour.

findings.text: Under the 2022 California Building Code, a restaurant or bar is Assembly Group A-2, and a space for fewer than 50 people is Group B. Whether the proposed occupancy group changes from the existing one determines whether a change-of-occupancy permit is required.

The existing occupancy group of the space is not shown in public records; only architectural plans or a DBI inspection establish it. Without the existing and proposed occupancy groups, whether a change of occupancy occurs cannot be determined.

No tenant improvements are stated in the concept profile. If the project involves only a license upgrade with no kitchen, seating, or structural changes, Planning may treat the use as a continuation of the 1988 CUA and no building permit may be needed.

expected_conditions.condition: The restaurant must operate and maintain the premises as a bona fide eating place, with at least 51% of gross receipts from food prepared and sold to guests on the premises, and submit records of the preceding year's sales to Planning on request.
expected_conditions.basis: Planning Code § 780.3(c)(2)(A) requires this finding for any restaurant serving alcohol in the North Beach Special Use District. All eight comparable agency referrals for Type 41 and Type 47 licenses in North Beach in 2019–2023 included or referenced the bona fide eating place requirement.

expected_conditions.condition: Standard CUA conditions: signage must comply with Planning Code Article 6 and complement the building's architectural character; odor control equipment must be installed and not applied to the primary façade; the operator must maintain the entrance and sidewalks per DPW standards.
expected_conditions.basis: The 2022 Type 47 CUA for 414 Columbus Avenue (51 meters away) imposed these conditions, which match the standard conditions extracted from other North Beach restaurant CUAs in the dataset.

expected_conditions.condition: The operator must appoint a community liaison to address concerns from nearby owners and occupants, and provide written notice of the liaison's name, address, and telephone number to the Zoning Administrator and registered neighborhood groups.
expected_conditions.basis: Required by the 2022 CUA at 414 Columbus Avenue and is a standard condition for eating-and-drinking uses in neighborhood commercial districts under Planning Code § 202.2.

expected_conditions.condition: The authorization is valid for three years from the effective date; DBI must issue a building or site permit within that period, and construction must commence and be diligently pursued to completion.
expected_conditions.basis: Standard validity and diligent-pursuit conditions appear in all recent North Beach CUAs, including the 2022 Type 47 CUA at 414 Columbus Avenue.

expected_conditions.condition: If the project results in unresolved complaints found to violate the Planning Code or specific conditions of approval, the Zoning Administrator may refer the matter to the Commission for a public hearing to consider revocation.
expected_conditions.basis: Standard enforcement and revocation condition in the 2022 CUA at 414 Columbus Avenue and other North Beach approvals.

filing_playbook.action: Confirm the zoning pathway and formula-retail status in writing with San Francisco Planning.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Request a pre-application meeting or a Letter of Determination from Planning stating: (1) whether the existing Type 47 license (ABC #372058, issued 2001) is still valid for this space or whether a new Conditional Use Authorization is required; (2) whether intensifying the restaurant without enlarging the space triggers a new CUA under § 780.3(c)(1)(B); (3) whether the business is formula retail under Planning Code § 303.1; and (4) what records the Department needs to confirm the space has not been abandoned for more than 18 months. Explain that the concept is to upgrade from Type 41 to Type 47 at an existing restaurant with no construction, no seating increase, and no hours change. Ask for written confirmation of the pathway before filing or paying any application fees.

filing_playbook.action: Engage a liquor license broker to locate and escrow a Type 47 license for transfer to 1309 Grant Avenue, or confirm the status of the existing on-file Type 47.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Type 47 licenses in San Francisco are quota licenses acquired by transfer, typically priced at $100,000–$450,000. Instruct the broker to confirm whether ABC #372058 (issued 2001) is still active and tied to this address, and whether it can be reactivated or whether a new license must be purchased. The broker will coordinate with ABC to determine whether the census tract's over-concentration (59 active licenses against 12 authorized) triggers a public-convenience-or-necessity finding from Planning or the Police Department. Make the purchase or transfer contingent on Planning's zoning sign-off and ABC's final approval.

filing_playbook.action: File a Conditional Use Authorization application with San Francisco Planning if Step 1 confirms one is required.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the CUA application (Planning Code § 303) with: a project description framing the concept as intensifying an existing restaurant that has held a Type 47 since 2001, with no space expansion, no seating increase, and no hours change; proof that the restaurant operates as a bona fide eating place (sample menus, a statement that at least 51% of gross receipts come from food sales, and a commitment to submit annual sales records on request per § 780.3(c)(2)(A)); photos of the existing space and floor plan; the existing ABC Type 47 license record or the purchase agreement for a transferred license; a statement that the business is not formula retail (or disclose chain affiliations if it is); and a good-neighbor policy. Request fee waivers if eligible under the First Year Free program. Schedule the required pre-application community meeting and 300-foot neighbor notification, and budget…

filing_playbook.action: File the ABC license application or transfer with the California Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control after Planning signs off.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the Type 47 application or transfer paperwork with: the signed lease, the entity formation documents (CA SOS registration), the seller's permit (CDTFA), the signed purchase agreement if transferring a license, Planning's CUA approval or written zoning sign-off, a 30-day public posting at the premises (ABC provides the form), and $2 million liability insurance. State that the restaurant is a bona fide eating place serving meals prepared on the premises, and that at least 51% of gross receipts will come from food sales. If the census tract is flagged for undue concentration, submit a public-convenience-or-necessity letter from Planning or the Police Department explaining that the transfer serves the public interest. ABC will route the application to SFPD and Planning for review; respond promptly to any requests for additional information. Expect 90–240 days including escrow and loc…

filing_playbook.action: Register the business and obtain core state and city permits.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Complete in this order: (1) EIN from IRS (same day, free); (2) LLC or corporation formation with CA Secretary of State (1–10 days, $70–$150); (3) seller's permit from CDTFA (1–14 days, free); (4) San Francisco business registration certificate from the Treasurer & Tax Collector (1–5 days, $55–$700 tiered by gross receipts); (5) fictitious business name statement with the County Clerk if the DBA differs from the entity name (1–35 days including newspaper publication, $60–$120); (6) workers' compensation insurance from a licensed carrier or State Fund (required from the first employee); (7) EDD employer registration if hiring staff (1–7 days, free). Keep the Business Account Number (BAN) from Step 4 on hand for all other permit applications.

filing_playbook.action: Complete the Department of Public Health plan check and obtain the health permit to operate.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: If any kitchen equipment, layout, or menu changes are proposed, submit a plan check application to DPH Environmental Health with: sealed drawings of the kitchen layout showing all equipment, handwashing and three-compartment sinks, floor/wall finishes, and the grease interceptor; the menu; proof of a certified food safety manager on staff (ServSafe or equivalent, $100–$250, valid five years); and the $828–$2,207 plan check fee (tiered by project scope; a continuation of an existing restaurant with no remodel is often exempt). After plan approval, schedule a pre-final inspection at ~80% completion and a final inspection at least two weeks in advance. The health permit ($470 application, $0 annual fee for 2026–28) is issued after the final inspection confirms the facility matches the approved plans and the certified manager is on staff. DPH will route the application to Planning for zonin…

filing_playbook.action: If seating 50 or more, obtain the Fire Department Place of Assembly permit.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the Place of Assembly application to SFFD Bureau of Fire Prevention (49 South Van Ness, Suite 560) with the approved building plans, occupancy load calculation, and $446 fee. SFFD will inspect the exits, fire extinguishers, emergency lighting, and any commercial cooking hood suppression system. Schedule the final fire inspection before the DPH pre-opening inspection; the Entertainment Commission also requires this permit for venues of 50+.

filing_playbook.action: Obtain ASCAP and BMI public performance licenses and train all alcohol servers in Responsible Beverage Service.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Sign up online for ASCAP and BMI blanket licenses (each ~$300–$2,500/year based on occupancy and music use; both catalogs are needed to play a general mix of music; licenses are effective immediately). Within 60 days of hire, every alcohol server and manager must complete ABC's Responsible Beverage Service training ($3 registration + $10–$25 course, 1–7 days) and keep the certification list on site for ABC inspections. All food handlers must obtain California Food Handler Cards within 30 days of hire ($7–$15, valid three years).

timeline_cost.notes: The timeline is 120–300 days and the government cost is $3,800–$18,000, both to approval of the Conditional Use Authorization and the health permit (the entitlement path given by the rules). These figures do not include the ABC Type 47 license process, which is listed as insufficient information. If a CUA is required, expect 6–10 months (180–300 days) from filing to Commission approval including pre-application community meeting, environmental review, 300-foot neighbor notification, hearing scheduling, and a 30-day post-decision appeal period; the nearest comparable Type 47 CUA (414 Columbus Avenue) took 270 days from filing to approval. The CUA application fee was approximately $2,747 in 2023–24, CPI-adjusted to roughly $3,150 in 2026–27, and can rise with construction cost; restaurants may qualify for First Year Free fee waivers. The health permit application is $470 (includes initial inspection) with a $0 annual license fee for 2026–28. Other city fees: business registration $55–$700 (tiered by gross receipts), fictitious business name $60–$120, sign permit (if new exterior signage) $300–$1,500, and fire Place of Assembly permit (if seating 50+) $446. State fees: entity formation $70–$150, certified food safety manager exam $100–$250, RBS training per employee $13–$33, food handler cards $7–$15 each, ASCAP+BMI licenses $600–$5,000/year. The Type 47 license itself, if obtained by transfer, costs $100,000–$450,000 market price plus ABC's transfer fees; that cost and its 90–240-day timeline are not included here because how the license will be obtained is not established. If Planning determines the project is a continuation of the existing Type 47 and no CUA is required, the timeline and cost drop to the health permit and ABC referral (roughly 30–60 days and $500–$1,500 in city fees). The day range is the time to obtain the approvals when they are granted; it is not a time to a denial or a withdrawal.
